---
title: "Flybys"
---

```{r}
source("_setup.R")
cands <- read_fig_csv("flyby_candidates.csv")
```

{{< include _sample_warning.qmd >}}

A flyby is a bird passing a station: signal strength rises and falls on each antenna
in turn. One line per antenna, labelled by the antenna's compass bearing, or by port
number when the bearing was never entered on motus.org.

**Why it matters for the farm.** The order in which antennas peak is the order the
bird passed their bearings. After installation this plot is the check that the
port-to-antenna map in the interface document is right: if peaks come in the wrong
order, a cable is on the wrong port.

![](figures/flyby_grid.png)

```{r}
#| output: asis
cat(sprintf("%d candidate flybys in the sample data (visits under 90 minutes, heard on at least two antennas, at least 20 hits).", nrow(cands)))
```
